key_insight: OUCH combines pneumatic actuation with a focused indenter to deliver controlled wrist stimulation, eliciting discomfort at approximately 89% lower applied force than a handheld pressure algometer in preliminary testing.
engineering_relevance: Designed contact geometry and a buckling spacer enable compact wearable stimulation with concentrated loading and skin contact only during actuation.
method: Stacked pneumatic pouch actuators drive a rigid indenter through a compliant buckling spacer.
Finite element analysis and a deformable testbed characterize contact mechanics and deformation.
Blocked-force tests, clinician evaluation, and preliminary perceptual testing benchmark performance against an algometer.
evidence_signal: At 200 kPa inflation pressure, estimated indenter contact pressure reached 18,500 kPa—over 25 times the algometer tip pressure—while testbed deformation was more localized near the surface and comparable at depth.
watch_item: Preliminary discomfort results do not establish safety or diagnostic validity for repeated use in patients with disorders of consciousness.
paper_title: OUCH: Objective, Uniform, Controlled Haptic Stimulation for Automated Neurological Assessment
